<!-- pr-reviewer: 49d0a3c2cb9675a22c2e0682bd7db1d12f00d322 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The metric G76 is right and well pinned. The inch G76 still makes the control cut one more pass than was verified, and the inch golden this PR changes locks that in.

### What looks good
- Correct reading of the word. `R` is written in the **first** block (`G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)`), so it is the finishing allowance, not the second block's taper `R(i)`. The second block still has no `R`, so the taper stays 0.
- Public lathe references give the same meaning: the first-block `R` is the finish allowance and takes a decimal point; `Q`/`P` take no decimal point and are in least increments; the second-block `Q` is the first pass's depth. With `R0`, the control roughs 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 and then finishes at 1.2 again, which is a fourth pass nobody verified. With `R0.4` it cuts 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2, the three passes that were judged.
- Units agree with each other in both programs. mm: `Q400` (whole µm) and `R0.4` (decimal mm). inch: `Q157` (0.0001 in, so 0.0157 in) and `R0.0157` (decimal in). Converted, both are 0.4 mm.
- The new record `finish_allowance` is the laid finishing pass's own depth (`thread_cycle.rs:59-66`). It cannot panic: `i - 1` is only reached with `i >= 1`. Alternating infeed and one-pass threads are refused by name. The `ALT` word is optional in the stream and in the file, so old streams and projects read back to the same bytes.
- The Tormach lathe goldens are byte-identical to main (I checked `tormach-lathe/thread_g76_mm.nc` and `thread_g76_inch.nc`). No other dialect has a G76 golden. Only the Fanuc-lathe goldens changed: `thread_g76.nc` (mm and inch) and the new `thread_g76_area.nc`.
- Hygiene: no process files, no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, no snapshot PNGs. `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #417` are present, and the subjects are conventional. New code has no `unwrap`/`expect`.

### Local results (head 49d0a3c2, already contains `upstream/main` f2b42e3d, so the trial merge was a no-op)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `lathe_post` | 7 passed |
| app `lathe_post_inch` | 6 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76` | 8 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` | 4 passed |
| app `lathe_post_tormach` / `lathe_post_tormach_thread` | 8 / 8 passed |
| app `turning_thread` / `turning_thread_infeed` / `thread_passes` | 10 / 4 / 5 passed |
| app `golden_cl` / `project_roundtrip` / `recorded_post_streams` / `posting` | 32 / 73 / 5 / 17 passed |
| camcraft-post (all suites) | 464 passed, 0 failed |
| camcraft-cl (all suites) | 49 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `turning_thread` / `turning_thread_cycle` / `turning_thread_infeed` / lib | 18 / 3 / 8 / 328 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutation checks** (`fanuc-lathe.cps` and `thread_cycle.rs`, reverted after each run):
| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `R` forced to 0 | g76, inch, schedule |
| `R` not converted to inch | inch |
| `R` written as a no-point increment (`R400`/`R157`) | g76, inch, schedule |
| inch `R` at 3 decimals (`R0.016`) | inch |
| `R` = first depth instead of the finishing step | schedule only (the default thread has equal values) |
| record finish = plan allowance (old behaviour) | g76, schedule, motion `turning_thread_cycle` |
| Fanuc alternating refusal removed | schedule |
| one-pass refusal removed | schedule |

### Requested before merge
1. **The inch G76 words do not describe the three verified passes.** See `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc:12` and `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps:858`. Each word is rounded to its own lattice on its own: `Q`/`P` with `incr()` to 0.0001 in, and `R` with `fu()` to 4 decimals. The control then works on the rounded words. Running this PR's own control model (`control_depths` in `lathe_post_g76_schedule.rs`) on the inch golden words `G76 P010000 Q157 R0.0157` / `G76 X0.378 Z0.315 P472 Q157`:
   ```
   k - d = 0.0472 - 0.0157 = 0.0315
   pass 1: 0.0157
   pass 2: max(0.0157*sqrt2, 0.0157 + 0.0157) = 0.0314   (< 0.0315, not clamped)
   pass 3: max(0.0157*sqrt3, 0.0314 + 0.0157) = 0.0471 -> clamped to k - d = 0.0315
   finish: 0.0472
   control: [0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0315, 0.0472]   laid/verified: 3 passes
   ```
   That is four passes instead of three: a 0.0001 in rub pass that was never verified. It does not gouge, but it is the same kind of mismatch #417 is meant to remove, and it is on a golden this PR edits. (Main's `R0` gives five passes, so this is an improvement, but not yet the claim.) `R0.0158` would give exactly `[0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0472]`.
   Suggested fix: in `onThreadCycle`, work out the control's ladder from the **rounded** words (`incr(FirstDepth)`, `incr(MinimumDepth)`, `incr(ThreadHeight)`) and write `R` as `k_w - (last rung)`. Refuse by name if that rung is more than one least increment from the record's `height - finish_allowance`. Pin it with an inch twin of `same_ladder`: `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes` run under `units(.., "inch")`, which today would fail on the pass count. The same rounding can happen in mm wherever a rung is off the µm lattice, so the check belongs in the post, not just in the inch test.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- A project saved before this PR with a cached thread toolpath keeps `finish_allowance: 0` in its cached record. It posts the old `R0` (one extra root pass) until the operation is regenerated. Is that acceptable, or should the stamp move so the cache shows stale?
- The flank-infeed Z sign and the end-Z shift (body "Not exercised" 1-2) remain unconfirmed from public sources. I agree neither changes the final form for a single-start thread. A Hub or real-control check of `thread_g76_area.nc` before the cut would settle it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
